findings.title: Sourcing before compinit still errors and never registers
findings.why_it_matters: If a user puts `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` in .zshrc before `compinit` runs (common in hand-written zshrcs and with plugin managers that call compinit late), `compdef` is undefined, so the new guard falls into the `_rg "$@"` branch at top level. Every shell startup prints `_rg:341: command not found: _arguments` (the same class of error as #2956), and rg completion is never registered because compinit only discovers #compdef files in fpath. The `! $+functions[compdef]` escape hatch exists only for ci/test-complete, but it cannot tell that harness apart from a real user sourcing too early. Keying the fallback on the harness's own `_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS` variable (and silently skipping or warning otherwise), plus documenting that the source line must come after compinit, removes the startup error without breaking the test harness.
findings.suggested_fix: if [[ $funcstack[1] == _rg ]] || [[ $_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS == (1|t*|y*) ]]; then _rg "$@"; elif (( $+functions[compdef] )); then compdef _rg rg; else print -ru2 'rg: zsh completion must be sourced after compinit'; fi  -- and add to FAQ.md that the `source` line (and the fpath line) must come after/before `compinit` respectively.
evidence: Scenario: .zshrc sources the script before `autoload -Uz compinit; compinit`. At that point functions[compdef] is unset, so the condition is true and `_rg "$@"` runs outside a completion widget.

Reproduced with `zsh -f` in scratch (vendor fpath dir removed so no packaged _rg exists): output `_rg:341: command not found: _arguments`, rc=1; after a subsequent compinit, `${_comps[rg]}` is unset, so rg has no completion.
FAQ.md's new text only says to 'add the following to your $HOME/.zshrc file' and gives no ordering relative to compinit, so this placement is a normal way to follow the docs.
The only caller that needs the no-compdef branch is ci/test-complete, which runs `( _RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS=1 source $1 )`, so the harness variable already identifies it.

findings.title: FAQ zshrc snippet includes literal `$ ` prompt prefix
findings.why_it_matters: The FAQ tells users to add the block to $HOME/.zshrc, but the block contains `$ source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)`. Pasted as written, zsh prints `command not found: $` on every startup and the completion is never loaded. The fpath snippet just above it has no prompt prefix, so readers have good reason to copy this one literally. Removing the `$ ` makes the snippet paste-safe.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the block contents to `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` (no leading `$ `).
evidence: Preceding prose: 'you can add the following to your `$HOME/.zshrc` file:'

residual_risks: Verified in scratch zsh 5.8.1 that: autoload via fpath+compinit registers _comps[rg]=_rg and the autoloaded body sees funcstack[1]==_rg; sourcing after compinit at top level, from inside a function, and via eval inside a function all take the compdef branch (source/eval push their own funcstack entry). Not tested: third-party plugin managers (zinit turbo mode, zsh-defer) that may source before compinit and so hit finding 1.

If a developer's ~/.zshenv runs compinit, ci/test-complete would take the compdef branch and fail loudly with 'Failed to get comp_args'. That is a loud failure, not a silent pass, so it is not reported.
testing_gaps: No automated check covers `source` of the generated script, either with or without compinit loaded. ci/test-complete only covers the no-compdef, _RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS=1 path.
